title: Borrowed Phrases
text:
Many English idioms come from horse racing, sailing, and warfare. Phrases such as 'hit the jackpot' or 'in the same boat' carry the traces of older occupations that have largely disappeared. Native speakers rarely reflect on these roots, yet the origins still shape how the phrases are understood.

Not every idiom has such a clear pedigree. Some arose in print, popularised by newspapers or literature, and their meanings shifted over time. A cautious linguist therefore separates phrases with documented sources from those whose history is largely a matter of speculation.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, which fields gave rise to many English idioms?
What may have popularised some idioms, according to paragraph two?
Why might some native speakers never reflect on the roots of idioms?
options: They rarely consider the origins while still understanding the phrases
The roots are unknown to everyone

questions.text: What does the passage imply about a cautious linguist?
options: They separate documented sources from speculation
